text: The current paper has a focus on impulsive choice, which is considered to reflect impulsive behavior as a result of delayed discounting (DD) and/or reflection impulsivity. Where DD is the tendency of devaluating delayed greater rewards in favor of immediate smaller rewards, and reflection impulsivity is the tendency to not collect enough information prior to a decision. Related to, but distinguished from DD, is delay aversion (DA) which refers to the avoidance of delays as a consequence of a negative emotional response due to delay overall [ 12 ].
source_label: Impulsive choice in individuals with comorbid amphetamine use disorder and attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder
